clue.text: Ravel, last of wet fish

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word wet is the one taken

parts.note: to fish with rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: An angler's damp catch, or perhaps a menu entry, with Ravel looking like the French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the composer, fitting the puzzle's theme, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to entangle or snarl threads, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Glass one may be dropping?

definitions.meaning: an acrobat who falls and rolls, one who tumbles

explanation.surface: A warning that a drinking vessel might be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking vessel without stem is so named, and so is a gymnast who tumbles or falls over.

clue.text: She abandons playwright after a write-up, an all-time low

indicators.note: in a down clue a write-up turns the remaining letters to read upwards
the word She leaves the playwright's name, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Richard Brinsley Sheridan, Irish playwright of The Rivals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A female abandoning a dramatist after a bad review, hitting rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' removes the pronoun from Sheridan's name, and 'after a write-up' reads what is left upwards, as this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything is its nadir, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lice high on combination of acid and alcohol in cheese

indicators.note: something high is intoxicated or off its head, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: an ester is the compound formed when an acid reacts with an alcohol

explanation.surface: Lice getting high on a chemical brew inside some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' shuffles LICE to LEIC; 'on' in a down clue puts it above ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Leicester is a hard English cheese named after its county, an example.

clue.text: Fiddle not half inspiring difficult child — that's the effect of music!

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the first piece takes the child inside
only half of the instrument's name is kept, its opening part

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin
a brat is an unruly child

explanation.surface: A half-hearted violinist is inspired by a naughty child, and that's what music does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' means breathing in, so the half-fiddle takes the child inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrato is the pulsing variation of pitch a player or singer gives a note, a musical effect.

clue.text: Composer on the case of correct decision

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, Italian opera composer

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word correct are its case, like a shell

explanation.surface: A composer ruling on a legal case and getting it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the case of' takes C and T, the outside letters of 'correct'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's finding or any judgment reached is called this, a synonym for a decision.

clue.text: Group has little time to invest in composer

indicators.note: to invest is to put something into, so the time goes inside the composer

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A group with little time to put money into a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a set of things made or handled together, a synonym for a group.

clue.text: Show remorse having put mint in sage I chopped up

indicators.note: the mint is put inside the jumbled letters
chopping up herbs breaks them into pieces, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: Polo is a British brand of mint sweet with a hole in the middle

explanation.surface: A cook regrets putting mint in with chopped sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' rearranges SAGE and I into A plus GISE, split around the mint. Polo is a British mint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to say sorry, an expression of regret or contrition.

clue.text: They've got something worse to broadcast about capital in Nairobi

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the capital letter
broadcasting scatters seed widely, so the letters are mixed
a capital letter is the first one, here of the city's name

explanation.surface: Holders of something worse going out on air about Kenya's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to broadcast' mixes WORSE around N, the first letter of Nairobi.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who possess things are proprietors or holders, so they have got something.

clue.text: Out of it, put to death

definitions.meaning: heavily under the influence of drugs

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for intoxicated by drugs and also means killed by pelting with rocks.

clue.text: New Testament suggested the coolest of times?

parts.note: NT, its abbreviation, is the middle pair of letters of the cold season's name, so the season's middle suggests it

explanation.surface: Something in the Gospels hinted at the coldest season.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: N and T sit in the middle of the cold season's name, so 'mid' plus that season gives the abbreviation NT. 'suggested' signals this.
explanation.definitionFit: The depth of the cold season is the chilliest part of the year, a playful description.

clue.text: Ultimately flat, instrument that's sharp

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of flat

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A musical comment: an instrument playing flat when it should be sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' and 'sharp' look like musical pitch terms, but sharp means pointed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant stem, something with a point.

clue.text: Grand work of Elgar, an exercise in music

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so the composer's name is reworked

parts.note: a scale is a run of notes practised as an exercise

explanation.surface: A grand piece by Elgar, like a musical exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work of' looks like a composition by Elgar, but signals the rearranging of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something large-scale is extensive or ambitious, which is what grand means.

clue.text: Sit alongside robin with huge bats

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go mad

explanation.surface: A robin perching next to some huge bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the flying animals, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something is to be next to it or border on it.

clue.text: In flaming, fire disturbed

indicators.note: the fire word goes inside the flaming word

parts.note: flaming has the colour of fire, red
to fire someone is to oust them

explanation.surface: Something set alight, a blaze disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like the noun for flames but is the verb meaning to sack.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or drive out roughly, so rousted means disturbed.

clue.text: For example, prepare an Ottoman composer to invade revolutionary Peru

indicators.note: the composer enters inside the jumbled country name
revolution overturns order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets

explanation.surface: Preparing a Turkish invasion with a composer storming revolutionary Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: An ottoman is a padded footstool; the capital letter makes it look like the Turkish empire. 'revolutionary' rearranges the country into two parts that surround the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to pad and cover furniture, and an ottoman is a stool that needs this.

clue.text: Composer is beyond preposterous

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other

parts.note: a tall story is a preposterous one

explanation.surface: A claim that some composer is beyond ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tallis was the Tudor English composer of church music, an example.

clue.text: Way of acting silly with feet in a pickle

indicators.note: a pickle is a mess, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Behaving foolishly with one's feet in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifestyle is the manner in which a person lives, their habitual way of behaving.

clue.text: Late actor has shifted tree to the left

indicators.note: the letters of has are moved around
in an across light leftwards means read backwards

parts.note: a fir is a conifer

explanation.surface: A dead actor has moved a tree to the left of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' turns HAS into SHA, and FIR read leftwards gives RIF.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Sharif, star of Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago, died in 2015.

clue.text: After scratching of head, nothing penned by composer is a disappointment

indicators.note: to be penned is to be enclosed, so the shortened word goes inside the composer

parts.note: Gabriel Fauré, French composer of the Requiem

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is scratched out

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A composer scratches his head after writing nothing, a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After scratching of head' removes the first letter of the word for nothing; 'penned by' places the rest inside the French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop or fiasco is a failure, something that falls short of hopes.

clue.text: Those who polish railway apparatus

definitions.meaning: people or pads that rub surfaces to a shine
the shock-absorbing stops at the end of a railway track

explanation.surface: Cleaners polishing railway equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Polishers are known by this word, as are the sprung barriers at the end of a train line.

clue.text: One offering a cut, as composer

definitions.meaning: Samuel ..., American composer of the Adagio for Strings

explanation.surface: Someone giving a haircut, rather like a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser who cuts men's hair is so called, as was the American composer Samuel Barber.

clue.text: Has that lady visited an illicit bar?

parts.note: she refers to a woman
to have been somewhere is to have visited it

explanation.surface: A question whether a woman has been to a drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has that lady visited?' is read as 'she been?', with 'Has' only linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking house, chiefly in Ireland and South Africa.

clue.text: Known leaders in baseball league, one entering competition after an upset

indicators.note: the leaders and the numeral go inside the competition word
upset turns the competition word over, upwards in this down light

parts.note: a cup is a trophy competition

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Baseball league leaders taking part in a contest after a shock defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: CUP upset gives PUC; B, L and I go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made public is known to everyone, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Scarcely any absent in curfew, unlike degenerate less fortunate

indicators.note: to degenerate is to decay into disorder, so the letters are mixed
these letters are missing from the curfew word

parts.note: few means hardly any

explanation.surface: Few people out during a curfew, unlike some degenerate who is worse off.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking FEW from CURFEW leaves CUR; 'degenerate' mixes CUR with UNLIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word for ill-starred, meaning having worse luck.

clue.text: Old man after a drop of cream with high tea

indicators.note: the old man comes after the other pieces
only a drop, the first letter, of the word cream

parts.note: up means high
pa is an informal name for father

explanation.surface: Father having cream with high tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high tea' looks like a meal, but 'high' gives UP and 'tea' is the definition. CUPPA is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is a cup of tea, the everyday British term.

clue.text: See 11
Instead, a general saying

indicators.note: the clue's first word is split as 'in stead', and its opening 'in' says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A general's proverb offered in place of something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Instead' as 'In stead': 'In' is the indicator, and the answer runs through 'steAD A GEneral'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a proverb or maxim, a traditional piece of wisdom.

clue.text: Brahms and Liszt in the spotlight

definitions.meaning: rhyming slang for drunk, the rhyme being on a slang word for drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Brahms and Liszt is British rhyming slang for drunk, which the phrase also means, besides illuminated.

clue.text: Tuesday 7th of September off — 8th of September past it then?

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are scrambled
the seventh letter of the month's name
the eighth letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A date puzzle: a Tuesday in September is cancelled, and the next day is past it.
explanation.walkthrough: '7th of September' gives B and '8th of September' gives E; 'off' mixes TUESDAY with B.
explanation.definitionFit: Food past its best-before marking is out of date, so it has gone beyond this date.

clue.text: Much bloodshed as one composer almost crushed by another

indicators.note: squeezed between, so the first composer goes inside the second

parts.note: John Cage, American composer of 4'33"

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A bloodbath as one composer is crushed by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of Arne; 'crushed by' squeezes the rest inside the second composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnage is the slaughter of many people, much killing.

clue.text: Composer's name for composer

parts.note: Carl Maria von Weber, German composer; the 's here means has

explanation.surface: A composer's name used for another composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Webern was the Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, an example.
